page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio designed for compute-oriented workloads. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 8.0 GB (2.0 GB per vCPU), supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are available. Local storage is bundled as a 150 GB NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute efficiency. In stress-ng single-core execution, the processor ranks in the top tier (3,394.17), matched by an upper-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 2,125.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.64 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory write throughput also registers in the upper quartile at 106.77 GB/sec. Across multi-core benchmarks, the system consistently shows mid-tier throughput, recording 13,418.26 in stress-ng multi-core and 6,739.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory and instruction sets, the PassMark CPU score reaches 11,266.24 and Redis SET performance delivers 10.08 million operations per second, both sitting in the middle tier.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge primarily in parallel memory processing, web serving, and database transactions under load. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations both place in the lower quartile, alongside a static web serving throughput rate of 4.4 GB/sec. Due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware and modest core counts, medium-tier machine learning inference is restricted, scoring in the bottom tier for 7B LLM prompt processing (11.93 tokens/sec) and text generation (7.98 tokens/sec).

With its combination of high single-core compute performance, dedicated AMD vCPUs, and local NVMe storage, voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is well suited for code compilation pipelines, build agents, continuous integration tasks, batch image and text processing, and CPU-bound utilities that do not require high memory density or GPU acceleration.
description: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is a compute-focused instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute series. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor at 2.0 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD. Advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators are enabled. Synthetic tests reveal top-tier single-core performance alongside strong large-block memory write throughput and compression rates, while aggregate multi-core metrics sit in the median tier. Because of its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio and absence of GPUs, performance drops in larger model inference and high-concurrency database queries. This makes the instance suitable for single-threaded processing, CI/CD runners, build automation, and general computational batch jobs.
